# GitHub Actions

Workflows set up Nix through the repo-local composite action `./.github/actions/nix-setup`, which owns the installer
version, the `GH_PAT` access token, the substituters list and the trusted public keys. Pass its `packages`, `channel` or
`extra-features` inputs instead of writing installer steps; `action.yml` documents each input.
Build jobs pass `cache: true`, which caches build results with hestia; leave it off elsewhere, since substituting and
`nix eval` never reach hestia's post-build hook. Nothing prunes that cache: GitHub evicts least-recently-used entries.

The agent workflows (`pi-bump`, `nix-bump`, `pi-dotfiles`) are siblings: each checks out the repo first, then shares
`./.github/actions/pi-agent` (nix, optional node, pinned agent invocation), and every prompt defers the PR mechanics to
`.github/prompts/agent-publish-contract.md`. The CI agent only reads its prompt — this file guides the agent that
maintains the workflows, not the agent that runs them. Check the siblings together: a change that fixes one
workflow usually applies to the others, and a change to the shared action or the contract must be reviewed against
every consuming workflow in the same change.
Only the agent workflows pass `GH_PAT` to `actions/checkout` so the agent can push as the repo owner. See the
publish contract for PR authorship. Other jobs rely on the default token; push-check is read-only.

Action references use version tags (`actions/checkout@v7.0.1`); `.github/workflows/actions.lock` records the exact
commit behind each tag, so a moved tag changes nothing until someone relocks. Local actions are referenced as
`$/.github/actions/<name>` (not `./`) so the lockfile covers the remote actions they use. The lockfile is generated by
the `gh actions-lock` extension; never edit it by hand:

- After adding or changing any `uses:` (workflow or composite action), run `just ci::lock` and commit the lockfile
  with it
- `just ci::lock --relock` advances moved tags to their current upstream commits; review the lockfile diff
- The `lock_check` job in `push-check.yaml` runs `gh actions-lock --verify` (locally: `just ci::lock-verify`). A stale lockfile otherwise
  surfaces only as a `startup_failure` with no check on the PR. Its `--pin vX.Y.Z` extension version is a manual bump point:
  raise it together with a `--relock`

`just ci::lint` runs actionlint (the `workflow_lint` job in `push-check.yaml`), with shellcheck of `run:` scripts off.
`.github/actionlint.yaml` silences its complaint about the `$/` form of `uses:`; delete it once a release accepts `$/`
(rhysd/actionlint#711).

Flake inputs are not action pins: the "Flake updater" workflow owns `flake.lock`.
